newsitem.title: UK: Storehouse H1 results seen rising.
newsitem.headline: Storehouse H1 results seen rising.

text.p: British clothing retailer Storehouse Plc's half-year results due out next Thursday are likely to be slightly up on the same period last year, analysts said on Friday.

Retail analysts forecast pre-tax profits between 35 and 36 million stg, up from the 34.5 million stg recorded this time last year. The half-year dividend is forecast at 3.3 pence, up 0.3 pence from last year.
"Profits should be up," said MeesPierson retail analyst Nick Bubb.
"The share price has been pretty weak in advance of the figures," he added.
The shares peaked early this month at 287 pence and have been falling steadily since then to close at 272 pence on Friday.
Storehouse was formed in 1986 from the merger of Sir Terence Conran's Habitat-Mothercare group with the Bhs chain of department stores.
